clue.text: Team with a passion for cricket here, as related by Dickens

definitions.text: cricket here, as related by Dickens

parts.note: fire is passion or ardour
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: A cricket club whose players share a real passion for the game, described in the style of Dickens.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket is the insect, not the sport: Dickens wrote The Cricket on the Hearth, so the hearth is where his cricket lives. The pieces come in the order FIRE then SIDE although the clue names the team first.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Dickens story the chirping insect sits on the hearth, the area round the domestic grate.

clue.text: Bazaar has a lot to be said for it

indicators.note: something to be said is spoken out loud, so the word for lot is heard rather than written

parts.note: one's lot is one's fate or destiny

explanation.surface: A remark that a charity bazaar has much in its favour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has a lot to be said for it' reads as the idiom for being worthwhile; in fact 'lot' means fate, and 'to be said' signals that FATE spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A summer fair with stalls selling goods to raise money is essentially an outdoor bazaar.

clue.text: Standing in line

definitions.meaning: standing here means status or position in a hierarchy
a line of soldiers or taxis side by side is a row of that name

explanation.surface: Someone waiting in a queue.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase about queuing, but splits into two meanings with 'in' as the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Status in a hierarchy and a row of people or vehicles share one word, as in taxi row or military grade.

clue.text: Lured by drink, find one in the kitchen

parts.note: lured, as into a trap, means snared
rum is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Someone tempted by alcohol goes hunting for a bottle in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'kitchen' is orchestral slang for the percussion section, not a room in a house, so 'one in the kitchen' is a percussion instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The percussion section of an orchestra is nicknamed the kitchen, and this rattling drum belongs there.

clue.text: Glassy-eyed after large whiskey's keeping the cold out

indicators.note: after places the word for glassy-eyed behind the word for the large whiskey

parts.note: a large measure of whiskey is a double
glassy-eyed means glazed, with a blank stare

explanation.surface: A drinker staring blankly after a big whiskey that warms them against the chill.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests whiskey as a warmer against the cold; the definition is actually about windows with two panes.
explanation.definitionFit: Windows fitted with two panes separated by a gap are insulated against winter chill.

clue.text: Cab has broken down in Arab quarter

indicators.note: a cab that has broken down is wrecked, so its letters with those of has are rearranged

explanation.surface: A taxi has broken down in the Arab district of a city.
explanation.definitionFit: The old walled citadel area of a North African city is the native Arab quarter.

clue.text: A sort of dancer appearing all over the place

parts.note: ... dancer performs energetic dances in a nightclub

explanation.surface: A kind of dancer turns up everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appearing' is a link. The answer, from French, means in abundance, plentiful everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived phrase means galore or in plenty, things found everywhere one looks.

clue.text: British workman accepting minimum pay is supported by both sides

indicators.note: accepting means the British workman takes something in, so these letters go inside

parts.note: an artisan is a skilled workman
1p, one penny, is the smallest possible payment, and 1 is read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A British tradesman willing to work for the minimum wage wins backing from both employers and unions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minimum pay' is 1p, one penny, with the digit read as I; it goes between B and ARTISAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A policy backed by two opposing political parties is described as having cross-party support.

clue.text: If in skirt colour runs on outside, moisten with this

indicators.note: on means the runs letter is added at the end
outside means the colour word wraps round the skirt containing if

parts.note: hue is a colour or shade

indicators.note: in places if inside the skirt

parts.note: a midi is a skirt reaching mid-calf
taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Instructions for when the dye of a skirt runs, involving dampening it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs' suggests dye bleeding from a skirt, but it is the cricket R; 'outside' wraps the colour round the skirt with if inside, making HUMIDIFIE before R goes on.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that adds moisture to dry air is used to dampen a room.

clue.text: From which one can't get a drink until opening time

definitions.text: From which one can't get a drink until opening time

parts.words: From which one can't get a drink until opening time
parts.note: reads like a pub before licensed hours, but describes a lockable stand for decanters whose bottles can be seen but not reached without the key, named after the mythical figure forever kept from water

explanation.surface: A thirsty drinker waiting outside a pub until it opens.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth a king was punished by standing in water that receded whenever he bent to drink; the locked decanter stand was named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: A locked stand displays decanters of spirits that cannot be poured until it is unlocked with a key.

clue.text: Little dogs run together for fluffy ball

indicators.note: run together means two copies of the dog word are joined without a gap

parts.note: a pom is a Pomeranian, a small dog; plural dogs gives two of them

explanation.surface: Small dogs chase about together after a fluffy ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorative tuft of wool, as on a woolly hat, is a small fluffy ball.

clue.text: Isaac's son's to run plant

parts.note: in the Bible Jacob was a son of Isaac
a run in a stocking is a ladder

explanation.surface: Isaac's son is going to manage a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' as a stocking ladder is British usage; 'plant' is the herb, not a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden perennial with blue flowers and ladder-like leaves is named after the biblical dream of a stairway to heaven.

clue.text: Attractive waterhole patronised

parts.note: a well is a hole dug for water
patronised, as a regular customer does a shop, means favoured

explanation.surface: A watering hole much frequented by customers.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned word for good-looking or handsome in appearance.

clue.text: Ominous, because of summons

parts.note: for can mean because of, as in famous for
a bidding is a summons or command

explanation.surface: Something feels threatening because of a summons that has arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: Threatening or menacing in appearance, as a grim and unwelcoming sky.

clue.text: Dark dress for those working late

parts.note: the dark is the night
a shift is a simple loose dress

explanation.surface: A dark-coloured garment worn by late workers.
explanation.definitionFit: The group of workers employed through the hours after dusk forms a team working late.

clue.text: More optimistic opener's taken out willow

indicators.note: the opener is the first letter, and it is removed

parts.note: rosier means more optimistic, as a rosier outlook

explanation.surface: A cheerier opening batsman gets dismissed near some willow.
explanation.walkthrough: Opener and willow suggest cricket bats, but the opener is just the first letter of the synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A type of willow whose pliable shoots are used in basket-making.

clue.text: Fresh sorrow producing expression of dismay

parts.note: food that is fresh is still good, not gone off
grief is deep sorrow

explanation.surface: A new sadness making someone cry out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' looks like an anagram signal but is simply a synonym; 'producing' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of surprise or alarm used when something goes wrong.

clue.text: Demanding thin porridge and fish

parts.note: gruel is thin porridge of oats boiled in water
ling is a long cod-like sea fish

explanation.surface: Someone insists on watery porridge and fish for a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhausting and arduous, as a tough schedule that wears one out.

clue.text: Raffish people uttering cheques

definitions.meaning: unconventional, artistic people with a disreputable air
Czechs, said out loud, sound like cheques; natives of the old kingdom at the heart of the Czech lands bear the name

explanation.surface: Disreputable types passing dud cheques.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uttering' means passing off forged money or cheques, but here it also signals that 'cheques' is spoken, giving Czechs.
explanation.definitionFit: Free-living artists and the people of one historic Czech region share a name.

clue.text: Arbitrary edict a king reversed, in practice

indicators.note: in places them inside the word for practice

parts.note: use means practice or custom

indicators.note: reversed means the letters for a king are turned back to front

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A tyrannical order reversed by a king when put into practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reversed' turns AK into KA, which goes inside USE.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree issued by the Russian tsar, now any high-handed order.

clue.text: Unfit before and after match — that's unpleasant

indicators.note: the word for unfit stands before and after the word for match, splitting round it

parts.note: to unfit someone is to disable them
to match is to agree, correspond

explanation.surface: A player declared unfit both before and after a game, which is a nasty business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before and after' splits the unfit word round the match word; 'that's' is a link to the definition. To unfit someone is an old sense of disable.
explanation.definitionFit: Unpleasant and unfriendly, as an ill-tempered person or a nasty taste.

clue.text: Birds to watch, say, without getting up

indicators.note: in a down clue getting up means reading the letters from bottom to top
without in its old sense of outside, so eg goes round the word for watch

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means
to watch is to see

explanation.surface: Birdwatching from bed, without rising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' is used in its old sense of outside. The container gives ESEEG, and 'getting up' turns it over because this is a down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Large web-footed waterfowl, the plural of a farmyard bird.

clue.text: Prima donna last out of bed

indicators.note: the last letter is taken out of the bed word

parts.note: a divan is a type of bed

explanation.surface: An opera star is last to get out of bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrated female opera singer, the leading soprano of a company.

clue.text: Eliminator bringing excitement

definitions.meaning: a preliminary race or round that eliminates weaker competitors
intensity of feeling, as in the excitement of the moment

explanation.surface: A qualifying round that stirs up a thrill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bringing' is a link between the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A qualifying race and intense passion share the word for warmth.

clue.text: Flowers one gets out of bed

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
someone who gets out of bed rises

explanation.surface: A gardener's bloom getting up in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants with sword-shaped leaves and showy blooms, often purple, are a familiar garden flower.

clue.text: An extra,'turning out as Evita, did

indicators.note: turning out means the letters of the phrase are rearranged into a different result

explanation.surface: A film walk-on part played the way Evita did it.
explanation.walkthrough: An extra suggests a film role, but here it is something added. 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance added in small amounts, as a preservative in food, is a supplement.

clue.text: Conclude harvest

definitions.meaning: to conclude here means to infer or deduce
to harvest crops is to collect them in

explanation.surface: Finish bringing in the crops.
explanation.definitionFit: To infer, as in 'I take it that', and to collect crops share the same verb.

clue.text: Ruling on parking in the club

indicators.note: on joins the ruling word to the parking letter

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs
regnant means reigning or ruling

explanation.surface: A ruling about parking at a members' club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the club' is British slang for expecting a baby, not a members' club.
explanation.definitionFit: Expecting a baby; 'in the club' is an informal British euphemism for it.
